# SFCC-83 + SFCC-84 — Build Plan

**Produced:** 2026-09-06 · **Gate:** `findings.md` (four passes, cleared at the 2026-09-06 adjudication)
**Base branch:** `feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component` (PR #85, open, unmerged)

## 1. Goal statement

Build the Recently Viewed rail and its full-history page per **SFCC-83** and **SFCC-84** (ACs in Jira
`customfield_10231`), designed in **`Zimmermann_Design_System_2026` component set `40000587:38471`**
(Desktop `40000307:12444`, Tablet `40000730:13363`, Mobile `40000538:25030` — all authoritative,
corroborated by PDP-template instances `7998:13508` / `8272:28947`), with SFCC-84's page from the
**provisional** `Zimmermann_Designs` `3332:35655` — following `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`
(token hierarchy) and `.claude/rules/components.md` (container/presentational split), and extending
**PR #85 / SFCC-236's** `ZimmProductCard` family via a **new `VARIATION_CONFIG` entry** (not a new
card), a **copy-first override of `recommended-products/`**, and **co-located `<name>.css.ts`**
recipes registered in `theme/components/index.ts`.

**Scope corrected 2026-09-07 against the real Jira AC text** (Marcel supplied the full verbatim
SFCC-83/SFCC-84 tickets; see "PLP surface" in §2 and the Open Questions for the full reconciliation).
This plan's original scope line — "follows `.docs/prd/search.md` §7.4 (PDP + Cart); PLP is out;
SFCC-83 AC 9 knowingly not met" — was written against the PRD, never checked against the ticket's
own AC text, and is **superseded, not merely refined**: the AC states plainly *"Confirmed surfaces
are PLP, PDP, and Cart."* PLP is real, in-scope, unbuilt work — see §2.
**No consent gating** — not a development-phase carve-out awaiting a later fix, but genuinely out of
this ticket's scope: Jasmijn's own dependency note ("move the consent acceptance criteria to a
separate user story") and comment history move consent ACs to SFCC-106. Must still be stated in both
PR bodies so a reviewer doesn't read the absence as an oversight.

**🔴 Data source corrected 2026-09-08 — Einstein is confirmed "Not Deployed" on every real
Zimmermann site (Open Question 6).** By Marcel's explicit direction, this build ships against real,
live Commerce Cloud product data sourced by this browser's own tracked view history instead — see
§2's "Interim data source" for the full design. A follow-up ticket (not yet created, Open
Question 18) swaps in real Einstein later; this plan's A3/A4/A6/B2 steps are written against the
interim design already.

## 2. Scale call

### Architecture fork — resolved: override `recommended-products/`, which removes the Cart port

Verified directly at `node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev/configs/webpack/overrides-plugin.js`.
`isFromExtends` returns true when the request names `@salesforce/retail-react-app` **and the issuing
file is not itself inside `overrides/`**. The plugin's own comment (lines 116–127): *"This will return
true if the issuer is a file in a base template... This allow the base template to import from
overrides."* Implementation: `this.extends.includes(pkgName) && !filepath.includes(issuerPath)`.

Base Cart imports at `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/cart/index.jsx:36`:
`import RecommendedProducts from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/recommended-products'`
— a package-path import issued from a base file, so it **is** redirected once our override exists.
Base Cart is itself loaded by base `routes.jsx` via a relative `import('./pages/cart')`, which is not
redirected — so base Cart keeps rendering and picks up our override for free.

**Consequence: the ~2,460-line Cart copy-first (`index.jsx` 1515 + 8 real partials ≈ 948) is not
required.** This departed from adjudication item #10 ("we only have to copy-first for cart"), in the
direction of *less* work. **APPROVED by Marcel, 2026-09-06**, on the evidence that this is already the
dominant pattern in this repo: nine component overrides shadow base paths and are reached purely by
the resolver (`icons` at 64 base import sites — and mandated by AGENTS.md — `responsive` 12,
`product-view` 6, `drawer-menu`/`list-menu` 2 each, `header`/`footer` 1 each). The single page port
(`product-detail`) exists only because base `routes.jsx` loads pages by *relative* import, which the
resolver never redirects — a constraint that does not apply to components. Open Question 5 is closed.

**Caveat:** this is a *build-time webpack* resolver. It runs in the dev server and production build
only — **not** Storybook (`.storybook/main.js` aliases straight to `node_modules`) and **not** Vitest.
So the Cart behaviour cannot be proven by any automated test in this repo; it must be checked in the
running app. That is why A1's pause is a hard gate.

Cost of this choice: the override module loads at **four base import sites serving eight rails**, not
five as an earlier draft of this plan stated:

| Base import site | Rails | Takes the new branch? |
|---|---|---|
| `app/pages/cart/index.jsx:36` | Cart Recently Viewed, Cart May-Also-Like | **Yes** (1 of 2) |
| `app/pages/product-detail/index.jsx:40` | *(shadowed by our own PDP override — 3 rails)* | **Yes** (1 of 3) |
| `app/hooks/use-add-to-cart-modal.js:30` | add-to-cart modal (`pdp-similar-items`) | No |
| `app/pages/product-list/partials/empty-results.jsx:20` | PLP empty-search top-sellers, most-viewed | No |

It is therefore a **faithful port plus exactly one branch**, keyed off
`EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED` (`'viewed-recently-einstein'` — the same string as
`CART_RECENTLY_VIEWED`, `constants.js:156,160`). **Two rails take the new branch; the other six must
render identically before and after** — a hard pass criterion.

**🔴 Correction, 2026-09-06 — the PDP row above is misleading, verified directly against
`overrides-plugin.js`'s actual source, not just this plan's earlier paraphrase of it.** The
table's "Yes (1 of 3)" for `product-detail/index.jsx:40` describes the **base** file's import —
but that file is shadowed by our own PDP override page and never loads. What actually matters is
*our own* `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx`'s import of `RecommendedProducts`, and
`isFromExtends` (`overrides-plugin.js:128-146`) returns **false** whenever the issuing file is
itself inside `overrides/` — its own doc comment says so plainly: *"This will return false if the
issuer is a file in the overrides dir."* Our PDP page's current package-path import
(`product-detail/index.tsx:59`) is therefore **not** redirected to our override, at all, regardless
of `Island`, scroll position, or Einstein data — none of which were ever the actual blocker.
Discovered live during A1's mandatory Cart/PDP verification (Marcel: zero marker fires on PDP even
after a full scroll to the bottom, while Cart fired correctly and repeatedly).

**Consequence, and why this isn't just a testing nuisance:** as originally planned, PDP's Recently
Viewed rail would never render even after A6 lands the branch — Cart would work, PDP would
silently not, and SFCC-83's PDP requirement would ship broken with no test catching it (no PR-time
E2E on this path either, per the Loop depth section below). **Fix, folded into A6 (Marcel,
2026-09-06):** change `product-detail/index.tsx:59`'s `RecommendedProducts` import from the base
package path to a relative path pointing at our own override, per
`.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`'s existing "Importing an already-overridden component from a
new component" rule — the exact same doctrine
A6 already applies to `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` below, just missed for `RecommendedProducts` itself
in the original draft of this plan. See A6's updated step and pass criteria.

Two of those six are on **PLP**, explicitly descoped at adjudication #2. The override *loads* there
but its branch never fires (those rails use `EMPTY_SEARCH_RESULTS_*` recommenders), so **no Recently
Viewed rail appears on PLP**. State this in the PR body so a reviewer does not read the override's
presence on PLP as scope creep.

Rejected alternative — re-homing the fetch into a new Zimmermann container: still needs a per-surface
caller, and Cart is a base page we cannot pass props to without the 2,460-line port. Buys nothing,
costs the port.

### Branch: ONE, single PR (Marcel, 2026-09-06)

**`feature/SFCC-83-84_recently-viewed`**, cut from `feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component`.

An earlier draft proposed two stacked branches. **Marcel chose a single branch / single PR to
maintain**, which is now the plan. Step IDs keep their `A*`/`B*` prefixes (they read as "rail work"
and "page work") but execute as one sequence on one branch:

> A1 → A2 → A3 → A4 → A5 → A6 → B1 → B2 → B3 → GATES

**What this buys:**
- **The AC 5 / AC 84-1 split disappears.** Those two ACs are the *same* requirement. On two branches
  the rail would have shipped with an unsupplied `seeAllHref` and SFCC-83 could not be marked Done
  until the second PR merged. On one branch the link and its destination land together — no
  interim state where the link points at a 404, and both stories close on one merge.
- One review conversation, one CI run, one changelog entry.

**What it costs, stated plainly:**
- **The four-team CODEOWNERS fan-out on `overrides/app/routes.tsx` (`CODEOWNERS:94`) now applies to
  the whole PR**, not just the page half. Every reviewer group sees the full diff.
- **The provisional-design page now gates the confirmed-design rail.** SFCC-83's rail is authoritative
  at all three viewports and corroborated twice; SFCC-84's page comes entirely from a provisional
  source. If the page's design is challenged in review, the rail — which re-skins two live surfaces
  and has no such doubt — waits with it. Accepted deliberately; flag it in the PR body so a reviewer
  knows the rail can be split back out if the page stalls.

### Loop depth

Two stories, ~22 files, one 236-line copy-first file. Mid-size build.

- **Full implementer → tester → scorer** on A2, A3, A4, A5, B1, B3 — where a silent wrong answer
  ships (a variation flag misread from Figma; an ordering/cap bug of exactly the shape the FED
  handbook's finding 18 warns encodes itself into a passing test; an AC-8 gate that never fires).
- **Implementer + scorer only** on A1, A6, B2, A7, B4 — their gate is mechanical (`tsc`, `npm run
  test`, a diff read); a tester pass adds a round-trip without adding a check.

**Deliberately dropped, with reasons:**
- **No Playwright/E2E.** Adding an allow-list group to `.github/workflows/qa.yml` is Tier 1 CI config
  (`CODEOWNERS:65`) — out of scope. Without it these paths resolve to `e2e_scope: skip` and there is
  no PR-time E2E run either way (`.claude/rules/testing.md` > Change-scoped E2E). State this in both
  PR bodies rather than implying coverage exists.
- **No page-level Storybook story.** No page in this repo has one; the presentational organisms carry
  the stories, matching `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/partials/*.stories.tsx`.
- **No new `theme/components/*Shared.ts`.** Both recipes derive media queries from `breakpoints`
  imported from `app/theme/foundation` — one source, two importers, no copied literal.
- **No visual-regression tooling.** None exists; Figma parity is checked by eye against named nodes.

### PLP surface — 🟢 DECIDED 2026-09-08 (Marcel): fold into this single PR

**Superseded, not refined.** This plan's original scope line ("PLP is out; SFCC-83 AC 9 knowingly
not met") was written against `.docs/prd/search.md` §7.4's "PDP + Cart" framing and never checked
against the ticket's own AC text. Marcel supplied the full verbatim SFCC-83 ticket 2026-09-07; its
AC states plainly: *"Confirmed surfaces are PLP, PDP, and Cart."* PLP is real, in-scope, unbuilt
work, not a knowingly-deferred gap — the earlier "Routed, not planned into" note calling AC 9
wrong-as-written (bottom of this document) is itself the thing that was wrong, and is corrected
there.

**What's missing.** Unlike PDP and Cart, PLP has no existing base call site rendering a
`RecommendedProducts`-style rail keyed to `EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED` /
`'viewed-recently-einstein'`. The two PLP-side consumers this plan's own architecture-fork table
already identified (`product-list/partials/empty-results.jsx`'s top-sellers/most-viewed rails) use
the `EMPTY_SEARCH_RESULTS_*` recommenders instead, and only render on an empty search — not the
general "you've been browsing" placement PLP needs. This means PLP needs a **new call site**, not a
branch inside an existing one — most likely a new `RecommendedProducts` usage added to
`overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx` or a `product-list/partials/` file. That path is
**Squad A territory** per `.claude/rules/squadA.md` — a different owner than every other file this
plan touches (all Squad B / shared so far), and that rule file requires notifying the Squad A Lead
before touching it.

**Not designed yet.** No Figma node in either the original set or Marcel's 2026-09-07 supply is
confirmed as "Recently Viewed on PLP" specifically — the closest candidates are the unread
`Zimmermann_Designs` `9086:*` family (see Open Question 15, pending Figma auth). Placement (top of
grid? after N rows? sidebar?) is undetermined.

**Decided 2026-09-08 (Marcel): "we're doing PLP as well."** Folds into this single PR, not a
fast-follow. This does expand the file manifest into a fourth owner and a page tier this plan
hadn't touched (Squad A pages) — the "spans multiple protection tiers" condition AGENTS.md Hard
Rule #10 flags — but the decision itself is now made; add a real file-manifest row (below) and
notify the Squad A Lead per `squadA.md` before touching `product-list/`.

**Still genuinely open: exact placement.** No Figma node anywhere in the supplied set is confirmed
as "Recently Viewed on PLP" specifically — not designed yet, not guessed here. Mechanically, the
new call site is a `<RecommendedProducts recommender={EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED}
.../>` added to `overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx` (or a `product-list/partials/` file,
if the eventual placement sits inside an existing partial rather than the page shell) — the same
mechanical pattern PDP/Cart already use, wired through the same interim data source as A6 (§2). The
open question is purely *where in the page* (top of grid? after N rows? sidebar?), not whether or
how it's wired. **Owner: Marcel — confirm placement before this specific file is written**, though
nothing else in this PR needs to wait on it.

### Interim data source — Einstein unavailable, ship against real browser-tracked history (Marcel, 2026-09-08)

**Why this exists.** Einstein is confirmed "Not Deployed" on every real Zimmermann site (see Open
Question 6) — not a data-quality nuance, a total absence of any engine to call. Rather than block
the whole build on a platform-provisioning timeline outside this team's control, Marcel directed:
ship the UI now against **real, live Commerce Cloud product data**, sourced by **this browser's own
actual view history**, tracked client-side — not Einstein, and not any hardcoded/mocked fixture
(AGENTS.md's "no mocking" rule is fully respected: every product shown is real and live-fetched,
only the *list of which IDs to fetch* is sourced differently). A follow-up ticket (not yet created)
swaps that one seam for real Einstein once SFCC-112 unblocks; everything else in this build is
intended to survive that swap unchanged.

**The seam, precisely — this is what makes the later swap small.** Two independent concerns, today
both interim, only one of which changes later:
1. **"Which product IDs has this shopper recently viewed?"** — today: read from browser storage,
   written by this shopper's own PDP visits. Later: Einstein's `getRecommendations` response. **This
   is the only piece the Einstein follow-up ticket touches.**
2. **"Given those IDs, fetch real product data and turn it into cards"** — a live Shopper Products
   `getProducts` call (`allImages: true`, `perPricebook: true`, `expand: [...]` — the same
   three-flag combination already confirmed correct three independent times this session: Einstein's
   own `fetchRecProductDetails`, the PLP quick-test mapper, and the `zimmproductcard-live-demo`
   branch) plus a mapper. **This is real, permanent work regardless of data source** — it's the same
   was/now-pricing (`getPriceData`) and multi-image (`imageGroups`) work B2 already needed (Open
   Question 16), not thrown away when Einstein arrives.

**What this revises (already-committed steps, not just new B1/B2 work):**
- **A4** — `useRecentlyViewedGate.ts` is renamed to `useRecentlyViewedHistory.ts` and extended: it
  already writes a session flag on PDP view; it now also **records the viewed product's ID**, not
  just a boolean. Not a protected/shared hook (not on either hook-protection list, single consumer
  today), so the rename costs nothing structurally — see A4's rewrite below. This is the one file
  where "browser/local it is" is literally implemented.
- **A3** — the mapper's input shape changes from Einstein's merged rec+product object to a plain
  Shopper Product from our own `getProducts` call. Its output contract and its own scope decision
  (image-only, no price, no gallery — A2's `recentlyViewed` variation is unchanged) do **not**
  change; only where the input object comes from does.
- **A6** — the `recommender === EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED` branch trigger is
  unchanged (the base pages still pass that same recommender prop regardless of what we do with
  it) — what changes is that inside the branch, `recommendations.recs` (Einstein's response) is
  never read; the new history hook + a real `getProducts` call are used instead.
- **B2** — same swap: the page container calls the new history hook instead of
  `getRecommendations`, and feeds the stored ID list (**capped at 24, not the rail's 5-item
  slice** — see the stored-history-cap note below, superseded from an earlier "full, uncapped"
  framing once the `getProducts` 24-ID limit was discovered) into the richer was/now/multi-image
  mapper already planned.

**Storage mechanics, per "browser/local it is":**
- **Guests:** `sessionStorage` — unchanged from A4's existing design, still correctly satisfies AC 6
  (session-scoped, cleared at session end).
- **Registered shoppers:** `localStorage` — a genuine, explicit, temporary deviation from both AC 7
  ("available on login from any device") and the ticket's own Assumption ("storage... handled by
  SFCC"). `localStorage` survives closing the browser (better than nothing, testable), but is still
  **device-local** — it cannot and will not satisfy cross-device continuity. This is not a
  workaround for that AC, it's an explicit, stated non-fix pending the Einstein follow-up — must be
  called out plainly in the PR body and to whoever signs off testing, not discovered by a confused
  reviewer. AC 7 should be marked N/A-pending-follow-up for this PR, not silently tested against a
  single device and called passing.
- **De-duplication / ordering:** viewing a product already in history moves it to the front rather
  than creating a duplicate entry — required for AC 2's "most-recent-first" to hold up under repeat
  views, and needs its own explicit test (view A, B, A again → order must be `[A, B]`, not `[A, B, A]`
  or `[B, A]` misordered).
- **Stored-history cap — RESOLVED 2026-09-08, then SUPERSEDED same day once the 24-ID fetch limit
  was discovered.** Original reasoning (Marcel: "how would this be treated if Einstein were
  available? do the same as that"): real Einstein has no client-supplied "how far back to
  remember" parameter, so this isn't a product/UX decision — `RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED =
  500` was set as a generous engineering safety ceiling against unbounded growth. **That reasoning
  is now incomplete, not wrong** — it was correct given what was known at the time, but didn't yet
  account for two facts discovered later the same day: (1) Shopper Products `getProducts` has a
  hard 24-ID-per-request limit (SDK's own doc comment, independently confirmed twice during Phase 1
  implementation), and (2) Marcel decided the Full History page caps its fetch/display at 24 rather
  than batching (see B2 below). Given Full History will **never** show more than 24 items and the
  rail never shows more than 5, storing more than 24 serves no purpose — nothing beyond item 24 is
  reachable from any UI this build has. **`RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED = 24`, superseding
  the `500` above.** This was caught by Phase 1's own implementer, who read this plan directly,
  found the contradiction between what it was told to build and what this section said, and
  correctly surfaced it rather than silently picking a side — exactly the discipline this plan
  asks for elsewhere. **Open Question 17 is re-closed at the new number** — no further confirmation
  needed; this is a direct, logical consequence of Marcel's own 24-cap decision, not a new
  independent judgement call.

**What stays exactly as planned, unaffected by this whole section:** A2 (variation config), A5 (rail
UI), B1 (grid UI) — all purely presentational, receive cards as props, and have never cared where
those props came from. This is the container/presentational split (`components.md`) paying off
exactly as designed.

**To verify at implementation time, not guessed here:** the exact `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`
hook name for a batch product-detail fetch (likely `useProducts`, plural, alongside the already-used
singular `useProduct` — confirm against `node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/dist/` per AGENTS.md's
own Gotchas note before trusting the name).

**Not a scope decision for this PR:** what the Einstein follow-up ticket looks like in detail (does
it reuse the `getProducts`-and-map layer, or fully replace it with `fetchRecProductDetails`'s own
internal enrichment?). Left for that ticket, once it exists — this section only needs to ship a
clean, honest interim, not pre-solve the migration.

## 3. File manifest

Tiers from `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md`, `.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md`, `CODEOWNERS` — **never**
`.claude/registry/*.md`. **No Tier 1 file is touched. Nothing is BLOCKED.**

### Rail work (SFCC-83)

| File | Action | Tier | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| `overrides/app/components/recommended-products/index.tsx` | CREATE (copy-first, 236 lines) | **Tier 2** | `pwa-squad-b` + `tier-2-approvers` + `tier-1-approvers` (`CODEOWNERS:104`) |
| `overrides/app/components/recommended-products/index.test.tsx` | CREATE | **Tier 2** | as above |
| `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.tsx` | MODIFY (union member + `VARIATION_CONFIG` row + docblock). **Docblock correction applied 2026-09-08** (Open Question 8, done) — the Hover-image-swap note's "chose Dani over a conflicting AC" framing was inaccurate; a dated correction paragraph was added, shipped behaviour unchanged | Tier 3 | `pwa-squad-a` + `pwa-squad-b` (`CODEOWNERS:176`) |
| `.../zimmProductCard/index.test.tsx` | MODIFY | Tier 3 | as above |
| `.../zimmProductCard/index.stories.tsx` | MODIFY | Tier 3 | as above |
| `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmRecentlyViewedRail/index.tsx` | CREATE | Tier 3 | `pwa-squad-a` + `pwa-squad-b` |
| `.../zimmRecentlyViewedRail/zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts` | CREATE | Tier 3 | squads only (`CODEOWNERS:186`, last-match-wins) |
| `.../zimmRecentlyViewedRail/index.stories.tsx` | CREATE | Tier 3 | as above |

### A4 — Recently-viewed history hook, plus the PDP write

**🔴 REVISED 2026-09-08 — renamed and re-designed, per "Interim data source" in §2. Read this whole
step before implementing; the original boolean logic below is no longer correct and would ship a
real bug if built as originally specced.**

Create `overrides/app/hooks/useRecentlyViewedHistory.ts` (was `useRecentlyViewedGate.ts`).

This still answers **finding 28** — the *original* concern was that Einstein's recommender returns a
two-product baseline for a visitor with zero history, so `recs.length === 0` never fires and AC 8
isn't implementable from the response. With Einstein out of the picture for this build, that specific
failure mode can't happen either way (there is no Einstein response to leak a baseline from) — but
the fix is still needed, now for a more basic reason: something has to track what "recently viewed"
even means without Einstein.

**The boolean logic changes, not just the storage mechanism — this is the one real gotcha in this
revision.** The original design was:

```
hasRecentlyViewed = sessionFlagIsSet || isRegistered
```

`isRegistered` was a deliberate short-circuit: trust that a logged-in shopper has *some* server-side
Einstein history even on a fresh device. **That assumption breaks entirely once Einstein is out of
the loop** — there is no server-side history to trust anymore. Built as originally specced, every
registered shopper would show `hasRecentlyViewed = true` unconditionally, including one who has
never viewed anything in this interim system on any device — gating the rail *open* with zero real
cards behind it. That's a real, shippable bug, not a hypothetical; it must not be carried into the
interim build. **Corrected logic:**

```
hasRecentlyViewed = recentlyViewedIds.length > 0
```

— true for both guests and registered shoppers alike, based purely on this interim system's own
tracked history. `isRegistered` still matters, just for a different purpose now: it selects *which*
storage to read/write (see below), not whether to bypass the check.

**New return shape:** `{hasRecentlyViewed: boolean, recentlyViewedIds: readonly string[],
markProductViewed: (productId: string) => void}` — the boolean is now derived from the ID list, not
tracked independently, so the two can never disagree.

- `markProductViewed(productId)` writes to `sessionStorage` (guest) or `localStorage` (registered,
  via `isRegistered` from `useCustomerType()` — the same hook `use-einstein.js:449` already uses) —
  called from the existing Einstein `useEffect` in
  `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` (lines 772–801), alongside the
  `einstein.sendViewProduct` calls already there (left untouched — that call is unrelated real
  analytics, not this build's concern). One import, one call, guarded by the same `if (product)`.
- **De-duplication / move-to-front:** if `productId` is already in the stored list, remove the old
  entry before prepending — never a duplicate, and a re-view correctly becomes "most recent" again.
- **Cap the stored list** at `RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED` (**24, superseded from an earlier
  500 same day — see §2** — matches the Full History page's own 24-ID fetch cap, since nothing
  beyond item 24 is ever displayable) — trim from the tail, oldest-first, on write.

**AC mapping, restated for the interim system:** `sessionStorage` is session-scoped and cleared at
session end — **AC 6**, unchanged. **AC 7 (cross-device for registered shoppers) is explicitly
*not* satisfied by this interim design** — `localStorage` is still device-local. This must be stated
plainly in the PR body and marked N/A-pending-the-Einstein-follow-up for this specific AC, not tested
against a single device and reported as passing. See §2's "Interim data source" for the full
reasoning — this is a stated, accepted gap, not an oversight.

**Confirmed 2026-09-07, not a frontend gap** (pre-dates and is unaffected by this revision — restated
for continuity): SFCC-83's own Assumptions section states *"the storage of Recently Viewed is
handled by SFCC."* The interim system above is a **temporary, explicit stand-in** for that
assumption while Einstein is unavailable, not a rejection of it — once the Einstein follow-up lands,
this hook's job reverts to a thin boolean/gate again and the real history moves back server-side, per
the original design intent this section used to describe.

**Superseded by the above, not applicable to the interim build:** the old "stated assumption" about
a registered shopper with genuinely zero Einstein history still seeing a two-product baseline
(Open Question 6's original framing) — that residual was specific to trusting Einstein's own
baseline behaviour, which the interim system never calls, so it cannot leak through here. It returns
once the Einstein follow-up is built, at which point Open Question 6's original text applies again.

**Pass criteria**
- SSR-safe: initial state `{hasRecentlyViewed: false, recentlyViewedIds: []}`, resolved in
  `useEffect`. No storage access during render. No hydration mismatch — the rail does not exist on
  first paint and appears after hydration. (Also good for LCP; the PDP rail is inside
  `<Island hydrateOn='visible'>` anyway.)
- Wrapped in `try/catch` — Safari private mode throws on both `sessionStorage` and `localStorage`.
  Failure degrades to `{hasRecentlyViewed: false, recentlyViewedIds: []}`, never an exception.
- JSDoc with `@returns` (`components.md` > Hooks).
- Vitest: empty storage + guest → `false`/`[]`; one ID + guest → `true`/`[id]`; empty storage +
  **registered** → `false`/`[]` (**the corrected case — must be tested explicitly, since this is
  exactly where the old short-circuit bug would have shipped silently**); re-viewing an existing ID
  moves it to front with no duplicate; writing past the cap trims the oldest entry; storage throwing
  → safe empty default; first render before effect → safe empty default.
- **Make each fail on purpose first.** The FED handbook's finding 18 trap is a test that passes
  because it was written against the only arrangement already correct — this applies doubly to the
  registered-with-zero-history case above, since that's precisely the case the old logic got wrong.
- The PDP change is exactly two lines (now passing `product.id` into `markProductViewed`, not a
  no-arg call). Nothing else in `product-detail/index.tsx` moves (AGENTS.md Hard Rule #5 — no
  refactoring upward).

- zm-implementer: Executes one step of a Zimmermann PWA Kit build plan. Use when a planned step needs to be implemented in code. Writes only the files the step names, and stops rather than expanding scope. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- zm-orchestrator: Scope and spec-conformance checker for an in-flight Zimmermann build. Use after an implementation step to judge whether the work delivers exactly what the plan specified — neither less nor more. Reports a verdict; never edits code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- zm-planner: Synthesises gathered evidence into an executable build plan for a Zimmermann PWA Kit story. Use after all sources have been gathered, when the findings need to become a sequenced plan with per-step pass criteria. Does not gather evidence itself and does not write code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, WebFetch)

- zm-scorer: Scores an implemented and tested Zimmermann build step and decides PASS or return-to-implementer. Use after the Tester reports. Judges quality against six axes; never edits code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- zm-tester: Tests an implemented Zimmermann build step across multiple angles and reports findings. Use after the Implementer reports a step done. Finds and reports problems; never fixes them. Dispatches its own sub-agents for parallel angles. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Agent)

The agent will provide both qualitative feedback and quantitative ratings on encapsulation, invariant expression, usefulness, and enforcement. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)
- vercel:ai-architect: Specializes in architecting AI-powered applications on Vercel — choosing between AI SDK patterns, configuring providers, building agents, setting up durable workflows, and integrating MCP servers. Use when designing AI features, building chatbots, or creating agentic applications. (Tools: All tools)
- vercel:deployment-expert: Specializes in Vercel deployment strategies, CI/CD pipelines, preview URLs, production promotions, rollbacks, environment variables, and domain configuration. Use when troubleshooting deployments, setting up CI/CD, or optimizing the deploy pipeline. (Tools: All tools)
- vercel:performance-optimizer: Specializes in optimizing Vercel application performance — Core Web Vitals, rendering strategies, caching, image optimization, font loading, edge computing, and bundle size. Use when investigating slow pages, improving Lighthouse scores, or optimizing loading performance. (Tools: All tools)
- zm-implementer: Executes one step of a Zimmermann PWA Kit build plan. Use when a planned step needs to be implemented in code. Writes only the files the step names, and stops rather than expanding scope. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Glob, Bash)
- zm-orchestrator: Scope and spec-conformance checker for an in-flight Zimmermann build. Use after an implementation step to judge whether the work delivers exactly what the plan specified — neither less nor more. Reports a verdict; never edits code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)
- zm-planner: Synthesises gathered evidence into an executable build plan for a Zimmermann PWA Kit story. Use after all sources have been gathered, when the findings need to become a sequenced plan with per-step pass criteria. Does not gather evidence itself and does not write code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, WebFetch)
- zm-scorer: Scores an implemented and tested Zimmermann build step and decides PASS or return-to-implementer. Use after the Tester reports. Judges quality against six axes; never edits code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)
- zm-tester: Tests an implemented Zimmermann build step across multiple angles and reports findings. Use after the Implementer reports a step done. Finds and reports problems; never fixes them. Dispatches its own sub-agents for parallel angles. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Agent)

When you launch multiple agents for independent work, send them in a single message with multiple tool uses so they run concurrently.
</system-reminder>

### B3 — Turn the See-Full-History link on

In `overrides/app/components/recommended-products/index.tsx`, pass `seeAllHref` (site-prefixed via
base `useNavigation`/`buildUrl` — the rail must not build the prefix itself) and `seeAllLabel`,
subject to the trigger rule.

**Pass criteria**
- **🔴 Trigger rule REOPENED 2026-09-07 — the prior flat-5 closure misreads the AC.** Both SFCC-83
  and SFCC-84's own AC text reads "exceeds the visible rail width" (verbatim, supplied 2026-09-07) —
  genuinely viewport-relative language, not a Desktop-only figure. A5's own card-per-breakpoint table
  (§A5) already documents that "visible rail width" is 2 cards at Mobile, 3 at Tablet, 5 at Desktop —
  so a flat `> 5` threshold means a Mobile shopper with, say, 4 cards (which already overflows their
  2-visible viewport) never sees the link at all. **Revised approach — a breakpoint-aware threshold,
  not a ResizeObserver:** add a second named constant set alongside
  `RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_MAX_ITEMS` (which stays as the render cap, unchanged), e.g.
  `RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_VISIBLE_COUNTS = {base: 2, md: 3, xl: 5}` mirroring A5's own breakpoint
  values, read via Chakra's `useBreakpointValue` (already this codebase's standard responsive-value
  pattern) to pick the active threshold. This keeps the "no ResizeObserver, no runtime DOM
  measurement" property the original decision correctly valued — `useBreakpointValue` reads the
  current breakpoint, not measured pixels — while actually matching the AC's per-viewport wording.
  **The render cap and the trigger threshold are two different constants doing two different jobs;**
  do not collapse them back into one, which is what produced the original misreading. The PR body
  must state this reading was chosen over both the old flat-5 closure and Confluence 04.2's "more
  than one product." **Open Question 1 is reopened, not closed — see Open Questions.**
- The href is correctly site-prefixed on a non-default storefront (check at least one non-AU prefix —
  AGENTS.md > Multi-site: never assume routing).
- Clicking navigates to the page; the page shows the same products the rail showed, plus overflow.

5	/**
6	 * SFCC-83 — resolves how many Recently Viewed cards should be visible for the current real
7	 * breakpoint. Fixes a real, live-confirmed bug (2026-09-10): `useBreakpointValue` can only switch
8	 * at this site's own registered Chakra breakpoints (`base`/`sm`/`md`/`lg`/`xl`/`2xl`), but the
9	 * rail's own card-width styling (`zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts`'s `DESKTOP_UP_QUERY`) switches to
10	 * Desktop sizing at 1024px — this component's own real Figma Desktop threshold, not this site's
11	 * shared `breakpoints.xl` (1280px). Calling `useBreakpointValue(RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_VISIBLE_COUNTS)`
12	 * directly (the previous approach) meant the item-count cap only ever stepped to 5 at 1280px,
13	 * leaving a 1024–1280px gap where the card row was already styled for 5 slots but only 3 cards
14	 * were allowed to render — see `RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_VISIBLE_COUNTS`'s own correction note
15	 * (`app/constants/index.ts`) for the full incident.
16	 *
17	 * Two raw `useMediaQuery` checks, not `useBreakpointValue`, because the Desktop threshold this
18	 * needs to match (1024px) has no corresponding entry in this site's registered breakpoint scale
19	 * to key an object against — `breakpoints.md` (768px) still correctly matches both this site's
20	 * shared value and the rail's own Tablet start, so only the Desktop half needs the raw-query
21	 * treatment. Checked widest-first (Desktop, then Tablet) since both are plain `min-width` queries
22	 * that both remain true well past their own threshold — a real 1440px viewport matches both, and
23	 * only the order of these checks (not a mutually-exclusive range) picks the right one.
24	 *
25	 * SSR-safe by the same construction `useBreakpointValue` already relied on: both media queries
26	 * default to `false` before the client-side match resolves, so this correctly falls through to
27	 * `RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_VISIBLE_COUNTS.base` (the smallest/mobile count) on the very first
28	 * render, matching this hook's two callers' own prior documented fallback behaviour.
29	 *
30	 * @returns The number of cards the rail should render/cap to at the current real breakpoint.
31	 */
32	export const useRecentlyViewedRailVisibleCount = (): number => {
33	  const [isTabletUp] = useMediaQuery(`(min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`);
34	  const [isDesktop] = useMediaQuery(`(min-width: ${RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_DESKTOP_BREAKPOINT})`);
35	
36	  if (isDesktop) return RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_VISIBLE_COUNTS.xl;
37	  if (isTabletUp) return RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_VISIBLE_COUNTS.md;
38	  return RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_VISIBLE_COUNTS.base;
39	};

import type { ReactNode } from 'react';
import { chakra, useMultiStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
import { ZimmProductCard } from '../zimmProductCard';
import type { ZimmProductCardProps } from '../zimmProductCard';

export type ZimmRecentlyViewedGridProps = {
  /**
   * Typed as `ReactNode`, not `string` — this component owns no copy/intl, the same discipline
   * `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail`'s own `title` prop documents for itself (build plan §A5/§B1). Styled
   * with `textStyle="heading3"` directly below, applied from the start rather than left for a
   * caller to pre-style — the rail's own `title` shipped once *without* this and had to be fixed
   * after live Storybook testing caught it rendering in the ambient body weight instead of the

  /**
   * A pre-formatted, already-pluralized node (e.g. "16 Items" / "1 Item") — this component does
   * not own copy/intl, matching `title` above and `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail`'s own container/
   * presentational split (`.claude/rules/components.md`). Build plan §B1: the item count is
   * mechanical ICU-plural-selector copy ("go for it" — Marcel, 2026-09-08), which is the calling
   * container's job (SFCC-84's Full History page container, not built by this step), not this
   * organism's. **Rendered exactly as received — never recomputed from `cards.length` here.** A
   * caller is expected to derive this from the same `cards` array it passes below; see this
   * component's own stories/tests for the "the two stay in sync when a real caller wires them
   * together correctly" proof this step's brief asked for — that proof lives at the call site
   * (story/test), not as internal recomputation, precisely so a future divergence between what a
   * caller *says* the count is and what actually rendered stays visible instead of being silently
   * papered over by this component re-deriving its own "correct" answer.
   *
   * **Styled differently from `title` above — corrected 2026-09-10.** The previous revision of
   * this comment claimed the same `textStyle="heading3"` / colour treatment as `title`,
   * "confirmed via the same `3332:37131` screenshot" — that screenshot is this component's own
   * PROVISIONAL design source (see this component's recipe file's own module docblock), and the
   * claim doesn't hold once checked against a real page-composition node (`9551:110758` Desktop,
   * `Zimmermann_Designs` file — one of the same three real page frames the "TITLE ROW PADDING"
   * fix already cites): the title is `Default/h3-strong` (matches `heading3` exactly — 16px,
   * medium weight, uppercase), but the item count is `Default/Body 2` — 14px, regular weight, NOT
   * uppercase, a visibly smaller and lighter treatment than the title, confirmed directly in the
   * node's own rendered screenshot ("RECENTLY VIEWED" in caps vs. "16 items" in lowercase). Now
   * `textStyle="body2"` (the exact registered match — `typography.ts`'s own `body2`: 14px /
   * regular / 18px line-height / 0 letter-spacing) with `color="var(--zimm-color-link-default)"`,
   * matching the node's own bound colour variable (`alias/color/link/default`) rather than
   * `text-default` — both resolve to the same hex value in this palette today, but the semantic
   * token is the one Figma actually binds, so it's the one that stays correct if the palette ever
   * diverges.
   */
  itemCountLabel: ReactNode;
  /**
   * Rendered in the exact order received — no sorting or reordering happens here, and (unlike
   * `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail`) no cap/slice either: SFCC-84's Full History page has no ordering AC
   * of its own, but per build plan §B1 "the page is the rail's overflow — same order or it reads
   * as broken", and the page container (not this component) is already responsible for capping

const ZIMM_RECENTLY_VIEWED_GRID_RECIPE = 'ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid';

/**

 * `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail`'s own `recentlyViewedCard.ts`, whose narrower image-only output cannot

 * unchanged by anything below. What DID change, this session (2026-09-07/08): the specific

 * on the provisional source's word alone —

 *     Bar desktop", 1440×75), which renders "RECENTLY VIEWED" (left) / "16 ITEMS" (right) —
 *     confirming both the title-left/count-right layout and the title bar's own content in one

 *   - **The `Sidebar` (`3332:35664`) child holds four stacked `Products Module Desktop` instances**

 *     structurally identical (four `Products S Desktop` instances each, 288×542, at

 *     states to design against.
 *   - **The `variation: 'plp'` decision** (see `cards`' own JSDoc above) is independently
 *     corroborated by a real, interactive prior-art branch, not just an AC-text reading — see this
 *     recipe file's own docblock for the full citation.
 *   - **The 96px horizontal card gap** (this recipe's own `GRID_CARD_GAP_DESKTOP`, Desktop only)
 *     was checked at two independent Figma sources specifically because it does NOT resolve to any
 *     bound variable — see this recipe's own docblock for the full "RESOLVED... checked twice,
 *     genuinely un-tokenised" citation. Tablet (80px) and Mobile (40px) each have their own,
 *     different, real-token values — corrected 2026-09-10, see that same docblock's "HORIZONTAL
 *     GAP" section for the full per-breakpoint story.
 * So: provisional design *source*, independently confirmed design *values* — both things are true
 * at once, and this docblock states both rather than letting the provisional-source caveat imply
 * the specific numbers below are unverified guesses, or letting the confirmed-values framing imply
 * the source ranking has changed.
 *
 * **This grid does NOT share its title row with `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail`'s own `title-and-link`**
 * (a deliberate build-plan call, not an oversight): the rail's header is Figma node
 * `40000538:20306` (h96/h56); this grid's is `3332:37131` (h75, one Desktop reading only, no
 * separate Tablet/Mobile node). Different components in Figma, so sharing would be a wrong DRY
 * call — see this recipe's own docblock for why no fixed header height is set here at all (unlike
 * the rail's own two-tier `HEADER_HEIGHT_MOBILE`/`DESKTOP`).
 *
 * Renders `null` for an empty `cards` array — the same defensive-leaf-component default
 * `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` uses (its own container owns the actual "should this exist at all"
 * decision; SFCC-84's Full History page has its own separate empty-state design, per build plan
 * §B2, which does not involve mounting this component with zero cards at all).
 */
export const ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid = ({ title, itemCountLabel, cards }: ZimmRecentlyViewedGridProps) => {
  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_RECENTLY_VIEWED_GRID_RECIPE, {});

  if (cards.length === 0) {
    return null;
  }

  return (
    <chakra.div __css={styles.container} data-testid="recently-viewed-grid">
      <chakra.div __css={styles.header}>
        <chakra.span textStyle="heading3" color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)">
          {title}
        </chakra.span>
        <chakra.span textStyle="body2" color="var(--zimm-color-link-default)" data-testid="recently-viewed-grid-count">
          {itemCountLabel}
        </chakra.span>
      </chakra.div>
      <chakra.div __css={styles.grid} data-testid="recently-viewed-grid-group">
        {cards.map((card) => (
          <ZimmProductCard key={card.id} {...card} />
        ))}
      </chakra.div>
    </chakra.div>
  );
};

Repo: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa (branch feature/SFCC-83-84_recently-viewed, already checked out — read-only investigation, do not edit/fix/commit anything).

Context: one of five parallel lanes reviewing the whole SFCC-83/84 "Recently Viewed" feature (rail + Full History page) as one coherent thing for the first time. Other lanes cover: (1) tsc/vitest/audit:tokens raw output, (2) the ZimmProductCard/size-chip component family's own styling/a11y, (4) structure/DRY/imports across the whole feature, (5) accessibility+Figma+AC conformance. YOUR lane is the hooks/utils layer's React/JS logic correctness, plus verifying a specific suspected duplication I (the coordinating agent) already spotted and need you to deepen — don't just take my word for it, verify from the actual code.

Files (all under /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/):
- hooks/useRecentlyViewedHistory.ts + useRecentlyViewedHistory.test.ts
- hooks/useRecentlyViewedRailVisibleCount.ts (no test file exists for this one as of last check — confirm and flag if still missing, per components.md hook conventions it should have JSDoc @returns at minimum, check that too)
- utils/recentlyViewedCard.ts + recentlyViewedCard.test.ts
- utils/recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts + recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.test.ts
- utils/recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts + recentlyViewedProductFetch.test.ts
- pages/product-list/productListCardMapper.ts + productListCardMapper.test.ts (base-file precedent, not this feature's own file, but directly relevant per item 2 below)
- constants/index.ts (RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED, RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_VISIBLE_COUNTS, RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_DESKTOP_BREAKPOINT)

**Task 1 — React logic correctness on useRecentlyViewedHistory.ts.** This hook returns `{hasRecentlyViewed, recentlyViewedIds, markProductViewed}`, derived via `useState` + a `useEffect` keyed on `isRegistered` (from `useCustomerType()`), reading from `sessionStorage` (guest) or `localStorage` (registered). Specifically check:
(a) **The guest-to-registered mid-session transition.** A guest views products (writes to sessionStorage via `markProductViewed`), then logs in (isRegistered flips false→true) mid-session without a page reload. The effect re-runs and calls `setRecentlyViewedIds(readStoredIds(localStorage))` — which, unless this device already has localStorage history from a prior registered session, silently DISCARDS the sessionStorage history the shopper just accumulated as a guest, with no merge/migration step. Is this tested anywhere? Is it a real gap? Read the actual test file and tell me whether this exact transition (isRegistered changing on an already-mounted instance, not just at initial mount) is exercised. If it isn't, write out (in your report, not as code) the minimal fixture that would exercise it and state plainly this is the kind of "prop that seeds state on mount receiving a different value on re-render" edge case this sweep is specifically supposed to hunt for.
(b) Confirm `markProductViewed`'s `useCallback` dependency array (`[isRegistered]`) is correct — does it ever read a stale `isRegistered` via closure, or is it correctly using the latest value at call time given the dependency array? Trace it precisely.
(c) SSR-safety: confirm no storage access happens during the render pass itself (only inside effects/callbacks). Confirm the very first render's return value is exactly `{hasRecentlyViewed: false, recentlyViewedIds: [], markProductViewed}` with no hydration-mismatch risk.
(d) Cap/dedupe logic (`dedupeAndPrepend`): re-viewing an existing id moves it to front with no duplicate; writing past `RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED` (24) trims from the tail (oldest). Read the actual test file and confirm these are each tested with a fixture that would FAIL if the logic were wrong (e.g. an order-dependent assertion, not one that would pass by coincidence either way — check whether the test actually distinguishes correct-order from wrong-order, per this repo's own "make it fail on purpose first" testing doctrine).

**Task 2 — useRecentlyViewedRailVisibleCount.ts.** Confirm it correctly imports `RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_DESKTOP_BREAKPOINT` from `app/constants` (not a re-declared local literal) and that its `isTabletUp`/`isDesktop` `useMediaQuery` checks are evaluated in the right order (widest-first) so a real desktop viewport doesn't fall through to the tablet branch. Note: there is currently no dedicated test file for this hook (verify this) — flag it as a should-fix given this codebase's own testing conventions require a test for hook logic with a conditional branch.

**Task 3 — recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts.** This wraps a batch `useProducts`-style SDK call. Check: does it defensively cap/slice its input ID list to the SDK's real 24-ID-per-request limit itself, or does it trust every caller to have already capped (recommended-products.tsx passes up to `RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED`=24 already-capped ids for the rail, but the Full History page container passes... check what it actually passes — read pages/recentlyViewed/index.tsx's own call to see if it slices before calling, or relies entirely on the fetch layer). If NEITHER the caller NOR the fetch utility enforces the 24-item limit defensively at the actual `getProducts` call site, and a future caller ever passes >24 ids, does this silently truncate, error, or misbehave? Trace this precisely, don't guess. Also check the `enabled`/gating logic (mentioned in recommended-products/index.tsx as `enabled: cappedIds.length > 0`) — confirm this exists and actually prevents a fetch with an empty array.

**Task 4 — the suspected mapper-logic triplication (deepen, don't just confirm the shape).** I found that `overrides/app/pages/product-list/productListCardMapper.ts` and `overrides/app/utils/recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts` both export identically-named functions — `selectGalleryImages`, `selectSizeChipValues`, `resolveOrderableVariant` (+ `ResolvedVariant` type) — and `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts`'s own comments say it was "ported near-verbatim from productListCardMapper.ts's own [pattern]." Both files also independently declare their own `const MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE = 'medium'` (a literal typed twice, not shared). `recentlyViewedCard.ts` (the rail's own, narrower mapper) has a third, similarly-shaped inline image-selection block using the same `filterImageGroups`/`MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE` pattern.
  - Actually diff the real logic of `selectGalleryImages`/`selectSizeChipValues`/`resolveOrderableVariant` between `productListCardMapper.ts` and `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts` — are they byte-for-byte identical modulo the input type name, or have they ALREADY silently drifted (e.g. one has a bug-fix comment the other doesn't, one handles an edge case the other doesn't)? Quote the specific lines that differ, if any.
  - Is there a shared module either of them could have imported from instead (check if `productListCardMapper.ts`'s functions are even exported/importable, and whether `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts` imports them or truly reimplements them)?
  - Report this as a DRY finding per `.claude/rules/conventions.md`'s "Apply DRY... extract to a shared utility once the same pattern appears in two places" rule, and per this sweep's own instruction that "a value typed three times with no shared source is a UNIFORM finding even when all three currently agree" (here: `MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE` is a literal typed 3x; the surrounding functions are a larger duplicated-logic pattern around it). Severity judgment is yours based on what you actually find (has it drifted yet, or not).

For every finding: file:line, what's wrong, which rule/AC it violates, severity (🔴/🟡/🔵), CONFIRMED or PLAUSIBLE, UNIFORM or ONE-OFF. State plainly what you could not verify (e.g. if you didn't have budget to run the actual test suite yourself — that's lane 1's job, but you can still read test files to judge whether the RIGHT fixtures exist even without running them).

<result>## Hooks/Utils Logic Review — SFCC-83/84 Recently Viewed

Read in full: `useRecentlyViewedHistory.ts`/`.test.ts`, `useRecentlyViewedRailVisibleCount.ts`/`.test.ts`, `recentlyViewedCard.ts`/`.test.ts`, `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts`/`.test.ts`, `recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts`/`.test.ts`, `productListCardMapper.ts`/`.test.ts`, `constants/index.ts`, plus the two callers (`recommended-products/index.tsx`, `pages/recentlyViewed/index.tsx`) and `theme/foundation/gridSystem.ts` to verify breakpoint claims independently. No test suite was executed — all "does this test discriminate" conclusions are from tracing the assertions by hand against a hypothetical wrong implementation, not from running vitest.

---

### Task 1 — `useRecentlyViewedHistory.ts`

**1(a) — Guest→registered mid-session transition. CONFIRMED, 🔴, ONE-OFF.**

The effect (lines 120-123) is keyed on `[isRegistered]` alone:
```ts
useEffect(() => {
  const storage = isRegistered ? localStorage : sessionStorage;
  setRecentlyViewedIds(readStoredIds(storage));
}, [isRegistered]);
```
On an already-mounted instance, if `isRegistered` flips `false→true` (login without reload), this effect re-runs and unconditionally overwrites `recentlyViewedIds` with whatever is in `localStorage` — with no merge, no read of the sessionStorage the guest just accumulated. If this device has no prior `localStorage` history, the shopper's just-built guest session evaporates from the hook's output at the exact moment they log in (a moment you'd expect *more* personalization, not less); `hasRecentlyViewed` can flip `true→false`, causing the rail to disappear or the Full History page to show "You haven't viewed anything yet" for a shopper who just viewed products seconds earlier. The guest data isn't destroyed in `sessionStorage` itself — just no longer read.

I confirmed this is **untested**: every test in `useRecentlyViewedHistory.test.ts` either mounts once as guest or once as registered (`mockCustomerType` called once per test, before the single `renderHook`) — none call `rerender` on an already-mounted `renderHook` result to flip `isRegistered` mid-flight. No test exercises a value change on a dependency that seeds state at mount, which is exactly the class of bug this sweep is meant to hunt for.

Minimal fixture that would exercise it: mount with `mockCustomerType(false)`, `act(() => result.current.markProductViewed('GUEST-ID'))`, wait for `recentlyViewedIds` to equal `['GUEST-ID']`, then call `mockCustomerType(true)` and invoke the *same* `renderHook` result's `rerender()` (not a fresh `renderHook` call) so the mounted instance sees `isRegistered` change without remounting, then assert on the resulting `recentlyViewedIds`. Under the current code this would show `[]`, proving the discard.

Also worth noting: this is **not** the same gap the hook's own docblock already discloses (localStorage's device-locality breaking AC 7's cross-device continuity) — that's a different axis (device→device). This same-device, same-session, guest→registered transition is undocumented anywhere in the hook's extensive docblock.

**1(b) — `markProductViewed` dependency array. CONFIRMED correct — no finding.**

```ts
const markProductViewed = useCallback((productId: string): void => {
  const storage = isRegistered ? localStorage : sessionStorage;
  ...
}, [isRegistered]);
```
`isRegistered` is the only reactive value read in the body, and it's the only entry in the deps array. `dedupeAndPrepend` reads only the module-level constant `RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED`; `readStoredIds`/`writeStoredIds` take `storage` as a parameter, not a closure. No stale-closure path exists — every render where `isRegistered` changes produces a fresh callback capturing the new value.

**1(c) — SSR-safety. CONFIRMED correct, well-tested.**

`useState<readonly string[]>(EMPTY_IDS)` is a pure initializer; both storage reads/writes live inside `useEffect`/`useCallback`, never invoked during render. First-render output is exactly `{hasRecentlyViewed: false, recentlyViewedIds: [], markProductViewed}`. The test at lines 84-103 proves this with `react-dom/server`'s real `renderToStaticMarkup` (not a mount simulation — effects genuinely never run under it), deliberately seeded with the *least* favourable case (`isRegistered: true` + pre-existing `localStorage` data) — a synchronous-read bug would fail this test. Solid.

**1(d) — Cap/dedupe logic. CONFIRMED correct, well-tested with genuinely discriminating fixtures.**

`dedupeAndPrepend` (lines 66-69) filters out the existing occurrence, prepends, then `.slice(0, MAX)` — correct dedupe-to-front and tail-trim. The re-view test (lines 142-155) asserts exact array order (`toEqual(['A','B'])`, not `toContain`/`toHaveLength`) after three sequential views — I traced a plausible wrong implementation (append instead of prepend) and confirmed it would produce `['B','A','A']` or `['B','A']`, both of which fail this assertion. The cap test (lines 157-174) asserts `recentlyViewedIds[0] === 'PRODUCT-NEW'` *and* that the tail id is gone — I traced a "trim from the wrong end" bug (`.slice(-MAX)` instead of `.slice(0, MAX)`) and confirmed it fails both assertions. Both tests are real fail-on-purpose-style tests, not order-agnostic ones.

---

### Task 2 — `useRecentlyViewedRailVisibleCount.ts`

**Test file exists — contradicts the stated premise.** `overrides/app/hooks/useRecentlyViewedRailVisibleCount.test.ts` exists (modified Sep 10 20:51, one file over the hook's own Sep 10 20:46) — this should be corrected in whatever tracking prompted the "no test file exists" note.

- **Import: CONFIRMED correct.** Line 3 imports `RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_DESKTOP_BREAKPOINT` from `app/constants`, not a re-declared literal.
- **Order: CONFIRMED correct (widest-first).** `isDesktop` (line 34, `RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_DESKTOP_BREAKPOINT` = `'64em'` = 1024px) is checked before `isTabletUp` (line 33, `breakpoints.md`). I independently verified `breakpoints.md = '48em'` (768px) and `breakpoints.xl = '80em'` (1280px) directly in `theme/foundation/gridSystem.ts:15,17` — both the hook's and test's assumptions about these values are correct, not just asserted.
- **JSDoc: present, satisfies components.md.** Lines 5-31 include a full docblock with an explicit `@returns` line — no gap here.
- **Test suite quality: solid, one cosmetic inaccuracy. 🔵 CONFIRMED, ONE-OFF.** The suite asserts the literal query strings (`'(min-width: 48em)'`/`'(min-width: 64em)'`, not `breakpoints.xl`'s 1280px) and the full base/md/xl cascade. However, the comment on the test at lines 40-44 ("returns md (3) when tablet-up matches but desktop does not — **the exact 1024–1280px gap the bug lived in**") mislabels its own fixture: `isTabletUp: true, isDesktop: false` corresponds to the 768–1024px range, which was never buggy under either old or new logic. The actual 1024–1280px regression case (both queries true, real ≥1024px viewport) is correctly covered — just by the *next two* tests (lines 46-50, 52-56), whose comments don't call out that they're the ones guarding the named regression. Coverage is fine; the comment on the third test just points at the wrong scenario, which could mislead a future reader trying to find "the test that guards the regression."

---

### Task 3 — `recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts`

**Defensive cap at the real call site: CONFIRMED present, independent of caller behaviour.**
```ts
const cappedIds = ids.slice(0, GET_PRODUCTS_MAX_IDS_PER_REQUEST);  // line 75
...
ids: cappedIds.join(',') as unknown as string[],                   // line 82
```
This slices *before* the `useProducts` call itself — it does not trust any caller to have already capped. Confirmed by direct read, and confirmed tested: `recentlyViewedProductFetch.test.ts`'s `'caps the request at the first 24 ids...'` (line 61) and `'products fetched beyond the 24-id cap are never returned...'` (line 74) both feed 30 ids and assert the request/response are capped to 24 on both the outbound and read sides.

**Caller behaviour, traced precisely:**
- `recommended-products/index.tsx:288-292` passes `recentlyViewedIds` from `useRecentlyViewedHistory()`, which is itself already ≤24 (`RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED`, enforced at the storage layer by `dedupeAndPrepend`'s own `.slice`).
- `pages/recentlyViewed/index.tsx:218` — `useRecentlyViewedProductFetch(recentlyViewedIds)` — **no slicing at this call site at all.** This container relies entirely on the fetch utility's own internal cap, and says so explicitly in its own docblock (lines 165-167): *"fetches real product data for those ids via useRecentlyViewedProductFetch (capped at 24 internally already — nothing further to cap here)."*

**Answer to "what happens if a future caller passes >24 ids": CONFIRMED, not a guess.** Because the cap lives in the fetch utility itself, not just at the two current call sites, a hypothetical future caller passing more than 24 would not error or misbehave — it silently truncates to the first 24 (most-recent-first, since `recentlyViewedIds` is already most-recent-first) and the tail is simply never fetched. This is Marcel's own documented "cap, don't batch" decision (the file's own docblock), not an accidental gap, and it's the one place in this feature that actually enforces its limit structurally rather than by caller convention.

**`enabled` gating: CONFIRMED present and correctly tested.** `enabled: cappedIds.length > 0` (line 91) and the `'empty ids -> disables the query...'` test (line 86) confirm an empty id list produces `enabled: false` and never fires a request.

**Minor, related observation (🔵, CONFIRMED, not the main ask but adjacent to it):** `RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED = 24` (`constants/index.ts:18`) and `GET_PRODUCTS_MAX_IDS_PER_REQUEST = 24` (`recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts:47`) are two independently-typed literals that happen to agree, cross-referenced only by prose comments on both sides, not derived from one shared constant. If the SDK's real limit ever changed, nothing would force the storage cap to notice, and vice versa. Lower priority than Task 4's finding below — flagging for completeness since it's the same general category (two places typing the same number).

---

### Task 4 — Deepened mapper duplication finding

I diffed the actual bodies, not just the exported names, across all three files. Conclusion up front: **the coordinator's suspicion is correct and I found more than the stated shape — including two genuine, already-live behavioural drifts**, not just a duplicated pattern that still happens to agree.

**4.1 — `MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE`/`COLOUR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID`: triplicated literals, still agree. CONFIRMED, UNIFORM, 🔵.**
- `MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE = 'medium'`: `productListCardMapper.ts:37`, `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts:133`, `recentlyViewedCard.ts:83`.
- `COLOUR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID = 'color'`: `productListCardMapper.ts:41`, `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts:142`, `recentlyViewedCard.ts:87`.

Six declarations of two literals, zero shared source. Per conventions.md's DRY rule and this sweep's own "typed three times, UNIFORM even if agreeing" instruction — this qualifies, even though nothing is wrong today.

**4.2 — `SIZE_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID`: a style inconsistency the duplication itself exposed. CONFIRMED, ONE-OFF, 🔵.** `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts:138` names this constant explicitly, with its own comment noting *"productListCardMapper.ts's own selectSizeChipValues, which this is ported from, uses the literal inline; named here instead since this is a fresh file."* Checking: `productListCardMapper.ts:170` does indeed inline `attr.id === 'size'` directly — arguably a standing conventions.md no-magic-strings violation in the *original* file, now visible only because its own copy fixed it without back-porting the fix.

**4.3 — `selectSizeChipValues`, `resolveOrderableVariant`/`ResolvedVariant`: byte-for-byte identical logic, no drift. CONFIRMED, UNIFORM, 🔵.** Comparing `productListCardMapper.ts:169-212` against `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts:287-325` line by line: the `.find`/`.map` bodies, the three-field object shape, and the `ResolvedVariant` type are identical in every token except parameter name/type. No behavioural difference found.

**4.4 — `resolveViewedColour`: not "similarly shaped," literally the same function. CONFIRMED, UNIFORM (2 files), 🟡 — sharper than what was asked.** `recentlyViewedCard.ts:126-129` and `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts:154-157` declare a function with the **identical name** and **identical 3-line body**:
```ts
const resolveViewedColour = (product: <TypeA>): string | undefined => {
  const fallbackVariant = product.variants?.find((variant) => variant.orderable) ?? product.variants?.[0];
  return fallbackVariant?.variationValues?.[COLOUR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID];
};
```
differing only in the parameter's nominal type (`RecentlyViewedProduct` vs `RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct`, itself a strict superset). This is the single cleanest, lowest-friction extraction candidate in the set — a plain `string`-in/`string`-out-shaped function needing no adaptation.

**4.5 — `extractImageSequenceNumber`: byte-for-byte identical across all three files. CONFIRMED, UNIFORM (3 files), 🔵.** `recentlyViewedCard.ts:101-105`, `productListCardMapper.ts:65-69`, `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts:167-171` are word-for-word identical (same signature, same regex, same fallback). Cleanest possible extraction — takes/returns primitives, no object-shape coupling at all.

**4.6 — `sortByImageSequence`: identical between two files, structurally-same-but-different-input-shape in the third. CONFIRMED, mostly UNIFORM.** `productListCardMapper.ts:76-82` and `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts:175-181` are byte-for-byte identical, both sorting `ZimmProductCardImage[]` via `.src`. `recentlyViewedCard.ts:107-115` has the *same comparator structure* (same stable-sort-with-undefined-passthrough) but operates on the raw `ImageGroupImage` shape via `a.disBaseLink || a.link || ''`, because it sorts before mapping to card-image shape rather than after. Not a bug — just means a verbatim 3-way extraction would need a shared key-getter/generic, unlike 4.5.

**4.7 — Colour-scoped image filtering core (`selectColourScopedImages`): identical filtering logic, one deliberate documented divergence. CONFIRMED, UNIFORM, 🟡 (elevated — see reasoning below).** The colour-scoped-`filterImageGroups`-then-viewtype-only-fallback two-pass block is textually identical in `productListCardMapper.ts:134-152` and `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts:241-264` (only the cast target differs: `ImageGroupShape[]` — a hand-rolled local shape — vs `ShopperProductsTypes.Image[]`, the real SDK type; the newer file is a genuine, acknowledged typing improvement, not drift). `recentlyViewedCard.ts:164-179` runs the *same* two-pass filter inline inside `selectPrimaryImage`, differing only in what happens after (`groups[0]?.images` → sort → take first single image, vs sort the whole mapped array and return it). The one real logic divergence — `resolveRepresentativeColour` (fuller, with a `representedProduct` branch) vs `resolveViewedColour` (fallback-only) — is explicitly documented in both files as intentional, driven by the input shape not having that field. I'm rating this 🟡 rather than 🔵 specifically because this exact logic has already needed two independent live-bug fixes (the "4673TS251 colour-mixing" bug and the "[2,1,3] sequence-order" bug, per the extensive docblocks in all three files) — logic that has already proven itself fragile is exactly where triplication is most dangerous for a *future* third fix landing in only one or two of the three copies.

**4.8 — REAL, CONFIRMED behavioural drift #1: `src` fallback operator. CONFIRMED, ONE-OFF, 🟡.** `recentlyViewedCard.ts:184`:
```ts
const src = groupImage.disBaseLink || groupImage.link;
```
uses `||`. `productListCardMapper.ts`'s `toCardImage:29` and `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts`'s `toCardImage:218` both use:
```ts
const src = image?.disBaseLink ?? image?.link;
```
`??`. These are **not equivalent**: if `disBaseLink` is present but an empty string (`''`) — a real-world API-quality edge case, not hypothetical — `||` falls through to `link` and can still produce a usable image; `??` does not (`''` is not nullish), so `src` becomes `''`, and the subsequent `if (!src) return undefined` (both mapper files) discards the image entirely rather than trying `link`. I checked every test fixture in all three test files for a `disBaseLink: ''` case specifically — none exists; the existing "falls back to link" tests only cover `disBaseLink` being *absent* (`undefined`), which `||` and `??` handle identically. <result>## ZimmProductCard family audit — findings

I did not use Figma MCP tools in this lane — per the brief, verifying against live Figma is lane 5's job; everything below checks whether the code's own comments are internally consistent with the code, not whether they're consistent with Figma itself.

---

### 1. The `recentlyViewed` variation — CLEAN, CONFIRMED

- `index.tsx:15` — `MediaOnlyCardLink = chakra(RouteLink)`, byte-for-byte the same pattern as `ZimmProductCardContent`'s own `ProductNameLink = chakra(RouteLink)` (`zimmProductCardContent/index.tsx:39`).
- `index.tsx:645` — `<VisuallyHidden>{name}</VisuallyHidden>` supplies the real accessible name.
- `index.tsx:646-675` — `ZimmProductCardMedia` receives no `onClick` in this branch (contrast `index.tsx:597`'s `onClick={handleMediaClick}` in the `showContent` branch) — confirmed correct, matching the comment's rationale (a real `<Link>` needs no click-passthrough workaround).

### 2. Recipe state exhaustiveness

- **`zimmSizeChip.css.ts` — CLEAN, CONFIRMED.** Lines 53-55 explicitly state Hover and Active/pressed are "NOT part of that variant set, so neither is implemented here," citing the four real states it does implement (Default `…125875`, Selected `…125874`, Disabled `…125873`, Focus `…130506`). - 🔵 **Note/open question — `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts:18-22` and `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts` (`close`:166, `arrowButton`:227, `scrollContainer`:80).** Both files justify their `_focusVisible` ring with "no Figma spec exists for focus on any of this component's three interactive parts... this gap was caught twice already in this build" — but neither file says anything, one way or the other, about hover or active/pressed for `nameLink`/`bagButton`/`notifyMeButton` (Content) or `close`/`arrowButton`/`scrollContainer` (Media). Unlike `zimmSizeChip.css.ts`, there's no explicit "checked, not designed" statement. I cannot tell from the code whether these controls have Figma-defined hover/active states that are missing, or whether Figma genuinely has none (in which case nothing's wrong) — flagging as an open question rather than skipping it, since I have no Figma access in this lane. - `zimmSizeChipGroup.css.ts` — clean; the component itself has no interactive role (layout-only `radiogroup`/`oneSize` parts), so no pseudo-state is expected here.

Grepped `hoverRevealsSizeSelector`, `hover: hover`, `:hover`, `:has(:focus-visible)`, `:focus-within`, `display: none`/`clipPath` across all 5 recipe files.

CONFIRMED via both the object-shape tests (`index.test.tsx:918-1077`) and a DOM-level focus test that specifically exercises the mouse-click-vs-Tab distinction (`index.test.tsx:1229-1313`).

<Box>
            {showNoResults ? (
              <EmptySearchResults searchQuery={searchQuery} category={category} />
            ) : (
              <>
                <SimpleGrid columns={[2, 2, 4, 5]} spacingX={4} spacingY={{ base: 12, lg: 16 }}>
                  {isHydrated() && ((isRefetching && !isFetched) || !productSearchResult)
                    ? new Array(searchParams.limit).fill(0).map((_value, index) => <ProductTileSkeleton key={index} />)
                    : productSearchResult?.hits?.map((productSearchItem) => {
                        // SFCC-83/84 quick test integration: ZimmProductCard's `plp` variation has
                        // no wishlist-toggle affordance at all (only `wishlist` variation has a
                        // remove/heart control) — the base ProductTile's `enableFavourite`/
                        // `isFavourite`/`onFavouriteToggle` (and the per-item `isInWishlist` lookup
                        // that fed it) have no equivalent here, so that per-item computation was
                        // removed rather than left dead. `addItemToWishlist`/`removeItemFromWishlist`
                        // themselves are untouched above — still there for whenever this affordance
                        // gets a real home on this grid.
                        const card = selectProductListCard(productSearchItem, formatPrice, buildUrl);
                        if (!card) return null;

                        // Renamed from `handleAddToBag` and re-parameterized 2026-09-08 (Gap 3
                        // fix): `productId`/`price` now arrive already resolved by
                        // `ProductListCard` itself, which is the only component that knows the
                        // currently-selected size chip. The `representedProduct?.id ?? productId`
                        // default this used to compute unconditionally is now that same
                        // component's own fallback for "nothing selected" — see its own
                        // `handleAddToBag` comment — so it isn't duplicated here.
                        const handleResolvedAddToBag = (orderableProductId: string, price: number | undefined) => {
                          addItemToNewOrExistingBasket([{ productId: orderableProductId, price, quantity: 1 }])
                            .then(() => toast({ title: intl.formatMessage(messages.addedToBag), status: 'success' }))
                            .catch(() => toast({ title: intl.formatMessage(API_ERROR_MESSAGE), status: 'error' }));
                        };

                        return (
                          <Island hydrateOn={'visible'} key={productSearchItem.productId}>
                            {/* Wraps rather than passing an onClick prop — ZimmProductCard exposes
                                no generic click callback, but a click anywhere in the card (the
                                image or the name link) still bubbles up through this wrapper. */}
                            <Box
                              onClick={() => {
                                if (searchQuery) {
                                  einstein.sendClickSearch(searchQuery, productSearchItem);
                                } else if (category) {
                                  einstein.sendClickCategory(category, productSearchItem);
                                }
