content.content:
/**
 * Guard: a multipart recipe's declared `parts` must cover every part the component actually
 * reads off `useMultiStyleConfig`.
 *
 * The failure this catches is silent, though not by the mechanism it looks like: `parts` does
 * not gate `baseStyle`. Probed directly against `ChakraProvider`, a recipe declaring
 * `parts: ['declared']` while carrying both parts in `baseStyle` and in a variant resolves to
 * `{declared: {...base, ...variant}, undeclared: {...base}}` — the undeclared part keeps its
 * full base styling and loses only the variant's. `parts` gates `variants`/`sizes`. The base
 * SFCC `theme/components/project/header.js` is that same shape shipping in production: 9
 * declared `parts` against 13 `baseStyle` keys, and the four it omits (`accountIcon`,
 * `arrowDown`, `signoutIcon`, `signoutText`) are each read, spread and styled by
 * `components/header/index.jsx` (lines 232, 255, 321, 323) today.
 *
 * So an undeclared part goes wrong in one of two ways, both quiet. If `baseStyle` covers it, it
 * renders correctly and then stops responding to variants and sizes — latent on a recipe with no
 * variants today, surfacing only the day someone adds one. If `baseStyle` does not, the read is
 * `undefined`, `__css={undefined}` is a legal prop, and the element inherits. Neither is reported
 * by `tsc`, eslint, an axe run, or a `play` that only asserts text. The first case is precisely
 * the "would survive a refactor invisibly if broken" case .claude/rules/testing.md says to cover,
 * so the corrected mechanism strengthens this guard's justification rather than weakening it.
 *
 * Comparing `parts` against the recipe's own `baseStyle` keys would not catch it: renaming a
 * part in both places at once keeps them consistent with each other and still breaks the
 * component. The component's reads are the only source of truth for what it needs, so this
 * walks the component source.
 *
 * Scope: `overrides/app/components/**` — every co-located `<name>.css.ts`, which since the
 * footer decomposition is where a component's recipe normally lives.
 *
 * It is not a whole-repo guard, and nothing else covers the remainder: the model is strictly
 * sibling-based (a recipe's `parts` are reconciled against the `index.tsx` beside it), so a
 * recipe that does not sit next to its component is out of reach. `theme/components/header.ts`
 * is the only multipart recipe in that position today and is therefore unguarded.
 * `theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts` does not pick it up either — that suite has no
 * parts-vs-reads check of any kind; it guards bare token keys and recipe namespacing.
 *
 * `READ_RE` recognises only the identifier `styles`, so a second binding in the same component
 * is invisible here: `zimmSubscribeModal/index.tsx` reads `chrome.actions`. That one is
 * deliberately out of scope rather than a gap to close — `chrome` holds *ZimmModal's* recipe,
 * so the sibling model would misattribute `actions` to `zimmSubscribeModal.css.ts`, which
 * correctly does not declare it.
 */

import { existsSync, readFileSync, readdirSync } from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';

const COMPONENTS = path.resolve(process.cwd(), 'overrides/app/components');

All five lanes are in, and I've cross-checked the disagreements against source myself rather than averaging them. Full reconciled report below.

## What I tried to falsify

I attacked five surfaces in parallel plus did direct verification myself on the highest-stakes claims: (1) whether the breakpoint-drift bug class (the one already found and fixed this session) has any unfixed siblings anywhere in the feature's 44 touched files; (2) whether the three image-selection mapper files that "agree today" have actually already silently diverged; (3) whether the ZimmProductCard family's own documented hover/focus-state fixes (`:focus-within`→`:has(:focus-visible)`, `display:none`→`clip-path`) hold everywhere or regressed anywhere new; (4) whether the whole suite/tsc/lint/audit-tokens gates are actually green, with raw output, not a claimed summary; (5) whether the accessibility and AC claims in code comments are true when read against the real code and real Figma nodes, not just internally self-consistent. Two things I personally re-verified that contradicted a lane's own conclusion (below) — both survived my re-check in the *stricter* direction, i.e. I found the problem was real where a lane had downgraded it.

---

## Internal sweep — does the feature agree with itself

**Recipe shape/registration — clean.** Every recipe (`zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts`, `zimmRecentlyViewedGrid.css.ts`, `zimmProductCard.css.ts`, `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts`, `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`, `zimmSizeChipGroup.css.ts`) uses the same `parts`-array/co-location/`Zimm*`-namespacing convention and is registered identically in `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts:90-91`. CONFIRMED (read all six, plus the registry).

**🔴 must-fix — CONFIRMED, UNIFORM (asymmetric application within the feature).** `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmRecentlyViewedRail/` has no `zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts` test, while its sibling `zimmRecentlyViewedGrid/zimmRecentlyViewedGrid.css.test.ts` exists. This looked like a minor asymmetry to two of the five lanes (one called it "a gap, not a failure — nothing to run"; the other downgraded it to a 🔵 note, reasoning "both recipes claim reconciliation via `recipeParts.test.ts`" — while admitting it hadn't verified that file's contents). I read `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts` directly: its own docblock states plainly **"`parts` does not gate `baseStyle`"** — it only reconciles the declared `parts:[...]` array against `styles.<x>` reads in the component's JSX, a pure naming/structural check. It asserts nothing about the actual computed CSS values inside `baseStyle()`. I also confirmed `zimmRecentlyViewedRail/index.test.tsx` mocks `useMultiStyleConfig` wholesale (same as Grid's own test does) — meaning **no test anywhere in this repo ever actually invokes or asserts `zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts`'s real `baseStyle()` output**: not the `CARD_ROW_SHARE_MOBILE/TABLET/DESKTOP` percentage math, not the two media-query breakpoint thresholds, not the header height/padding values. This is the single most bug-fixed file in the whole feature this session (three separate documented same-day live fixes: card sizing, header padding, the 1024/1280px breakpoint mismatch) — all three were caught by manual/live testing, none by an automated test — and it remains the one recipe in the pair with zero regression protection of its own computed values, despite its sibling Grid receiving exactly that protection after an analogous bug. Where the two lanes disagreed, going to source resolved it in favor of treating this as real, not cosmetic.

**🟡 should-fix — CONFIRMED, UNIFORM, and this is the headline finding of the whole sweep.** Three files independently reimplement the same non-trivial image/size-chip mapping logic instead of sharing it: `overrides/app/pages/product-list/productListCardMapper.ts`, `overrides/app/utils/recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts` (own docblock admits: *"ported near-verbatim... not imported"*), and `overrides/app/utils/recentlyViewedCard.ts`. All three independently declare `const MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE = 'medium'` and `COLOUR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID = 'color'` (six declarations of two literals, zero shared source — a UNIFORM finding "even when all three currently agree," exactly the pattern this phase exists to catch). Critically, this has **already silently drifted, twice, not just theoretically at risk**:
- `recentlyViewedCard.ts:184` uses `groupImage.disBaseLink || groupImage.link`; the other two files' `toCardImage` use `image?.disBaseLink ?? image?.link` (`productListCardMapper.ts:29`, `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts:218`). `||` and `??` disagree on an empty-string `disBaseLink` — a real API-quality edge case none of the three test suites cover in either direction.
- Alt-text non-empty enforcement is three different strategies: `recentlyViewedCard.ts:189` trims first (`.trim() || productName`, correctly catches whitespace-only alt); `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts:385` does not (`firstImage.alt || product.name`, so `"   "` would ship as the accessible name, violating this same component family's own "required non-empty, meaningful alt" contract); `productListCardMapper.ts`'s `selectProductListCard:289` has no enforcement at all beyond `toCardImage`'s bare `?? ''`.
Both are un-tested divergences today, not proven-live incidents against real Zimmermann data — that's why this is 🟡 not 🔴 — but they are real, current, and exactly the "kept in sync by a comment, not a shared source" shape the task called out by name.

**🟡 should-fix, CONFIRMED, UNIFORM (same shape as the already-fixed breakpoint bug).** `overrides/app/routes.tsx:83-85` hand-types `path: '/recently-viewed'` as a raw string rather than importing `RECENTLY_VIEWED_ROUTE` — the constant's own comment at `constants/index.ts:20-24` states its whole purpose is to avoid exactly this ("so the link has one canonical value to import rather than a second hand-typed copy"). Verified directly — `routes.tsx` imports nothing from `app/constants`.

**🟡 should-fix, CONFIRMED, UNIFORM.** Two independently-typed `24`s: `constants/index.ts:18` (`RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED`) and `recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts:47` (`GET_PRODUCTS_MAX_IDS_PER_REQUEST`), which the constants file's own comment explicitly frames as one fact ("matching the Shopper Products endpoint's own hard per-request ID limit"), not two independent decisions. Found independently by two separate lanes — doubly confirmed.

**🟡 should-fix, CONFIRMED, ONE-OFF.** `product-detail/index.tsx:1005-1008`'s pre-existing (SFCC-731) `marginX={{base: 'calc(-1 * var(--zimm-grid-margin-mobile))', xl: 'calc(-1 * var(--zimm-grid-margin-desktop))'}}` is mathematically and semantically identical to the brand-new `APP_MAIN_BLEED_MX` constant this session added specifically to name this exact cancellation — but the pre-existing spot was never migrated to use it. Verified directly.

**🟢 Positive, verified findings** worth stating plainly rather than only listing problems: `useRecentlyViewedRailVisibleCount.ts`/`recommended-products/index.tsx`'s shared Desktop-threshold constant is genuinely single-sourced now (I checked this myself before any lane ran); `recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts:95-98` correctly re-orders the batch API's response back into requested-ID order via a keyed `Map` before returning — this defends AC 2's ordering guarantee against an API that doesn't promise response order, and is tested with a deliberately-adversarial fixture (API returns B before A); the 24-ID cap is enforced defensively at the actual fetch call site regardless of caller discipline; `PAGE_CONTENT_BLEED_MX`/`APP_MAIN_BLEED_MX` call sites otherwise match their own doc-comments exactly; and Chakra's own `SimpleGrid` (used by PLP) already includes the `minmax(0,1fr)` guard that `zimmRecentlyViewedGrid.css.ts` had to add by hand, so PLP's grid was never exposed to the sibling hover-track-growth bug.

---

## External sweep — does the shared shape conform

**`.claude/rules/*` conformance.** `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0. `npm run test`: 1298/1298 pass, `recipeGuards.test.ts` passes. `npm run lint`: 0 errors, 21 warnings inside feature-scope files (all pre-existing-style nits — unused destructured vars, template-literal type warnings — one pair, `addItemToWishlist`/`removeItemFromWishlist` in `product-list/index.tsx:339,390`, is a lint warning but is explicitly self-documented in an adjacent comment at line 699 as intentional, kept for a future affordance, not a silent gap). `npm run audit:tokens`: zero unacknowledged findings in this feature's files; 8 newly-introduced acknowledged/pending entries, all correctly commented per the script's own vocabulary. `npm run build` exits 0, new route compiles clean. No bare Chakra token keys, no un-commented raw hex/px/rem/em, and no semantic-token/property mismatches found anywhere in the card family or the two new organisms.

**🔴 must-fix, CONFIRMED.** `overrides/app/pages/recentlyViewed/index.tsx` — the one genuinely new, standalone route this feature ships — has **zero real heading elements** in either its empty or populated branch (no `Heading` import at all; verified directly). This breaks an established, deliberate pattern this same codebase already follows on its sibling pages: `product-list/index.tsx:807` (`<Heading as="h1">`) and `product-detail/index.tsx:975` (`<Heading as="h1" srOnly>`). On the populated branch this is compounded, not just an absence: up to 24 real `<h3>` product-name headings render (via `ZimmProductCardContent`) with nothing above them in the tree — a broken hierarchy. AGENTS.md explicitly targets WCAG 2.2 AA; this is SC 1.3.1/2.4.6, and the fix pattern already exists one page-type over, so there's no ambiguity about what "correct" looks like here.

**🟡 should-fix, CONFIRMED, and important nuance for scoring.** Both new organisms render their own section title as `<chakra.span textStyle="heading3">` — `zimmRecentlyViewedRail/index.tsx:122` and `zimmRecentlyViewedGrid/index.tsx:144` — with no real heading semantics, so screen-reader heading-navigation never surfaces "Recently Viewed." I checked whether this is a fresh mistake unique to this feature or an existing pattern: `zimmSubscribeSection/index.tsx:60` and `footer/footerNavColumn/index.tsx:52` both do the identical thing (`<chakra.p>` standing in for a section heading). **This is UNIFORM with a wider, pre-existing organism-level convention in this codebase, not something SFCC-83/84 invented** — worth surfacing up a level as a systemic gap rather than scoring this feature as the sole owner of it, but it's still real and still worth fixing given the page-level `Heading as="h1"` pattern already exists to borrow from.

**🟡 should-fix, CONFIRMED (I read the recipe directly).** `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts:93-96`'s hover/on-model image-swap crossfade is gated on `[HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY] '&:hover ...'` only — no `:has(:focus-visible)` pairing, unlike every other hover-reveal in this same file family (price, size-selector, notify-me, carousel), which all pair the two specifically because of a keyboard-parity bug this codebase already found and fixed once (Fix H). A keyboard-only user tabbing into the card never sees the swapped photo a mouse-hovering user does. 🟡 not 🔴 because both images stay in the DOM with distinct real `alt` text regardless of state — decorative-parity gap, not an operability failure.

**Figma fidelity — reachable, and independently spot-checked, not skipped.** Live MCP access confirmed working this run. All 8 named nodes resolve (none deleted/stale). Every specific numeric claim that could be checked without `get_design_context` matched the code exactly: Rail's Desktop composition (`40000307:12444`) really is exactly 2 children with zero gap between 5 image-only cards; the Full History page's header padding (40/32/20px per breakpoint) matches the recipe's claims at all three breakpoints; the reserved 112px of blank footer-clearance space was independently re-confirmed correct at Desktop/Tablet/Mobile, not just the one breakpoint the code comment cites. What could **not** be verified even with working Figma access: the rail's "fluid `flex:1 0 0`, not fixed-width" claim and its specific 1024px Desktop-threshold claim both require `get_design_context` (gated behind an implementation skill, correctly not invoked for a read-only pass) — these two specific numeric claims are taken on the recipe's own citation, not independently re-proven.

**Exemplar PR — none is named for this whole feature, stated plainly rather than guessed.** `plan.md` names three different reference points for three different sub-decisions, not one exemplar to follow throughout: the branch this was cut from (`feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component`, PR #85, still open/unmerged); `feature/zimmproductcard-live-demo`'s mapper/section as prior art for A3/B1, with an explicit instruction to "port the approach, do not import it" (which is precisely why the mapper-triplication finding above exists — the plan itself chose the pattern that produces this DRY tension); and the footer decomposition as the co-location-pattern reference per `overrideStyling.md`. No single PR governs the whole feature's shape.

---

## Reconciling the two lane disagreements found

1. **Rail's missing `.css.test.ts`** — lane 1 called it a non-failing gap, lane 4 downgraded it to a 🔵 "just an inconsistency" on an unverified assumption. Reading `recipeParts.test.ts` directly settled it: that file cannot substitute for a `.css.test.ts` (it doesn't touch `baseStyle()` at all), so I elevated this to 🔴 above.
2. **`useRecentlyViewedRailVisibleCount.test.ts`** — I initially briefed a lane on a stale premise ("no test file exists"); that lane caught and corrected it, and I independently re-verified the test file exists (`ls` shows it, timestamped after the hook itself). No real disagreement — just my own initial briefing being wrong, corrected before it could become a false finding.

## What I could not verify

Nothing here was checked in a real running browser or Storybook instance — `npm start` is forbidden to me per this repo's own AGENTS.md, and no lane launched Storybook either, so every claim above is static-analysis-plus-Figma-metadata, not a rendered-pixel check. Specifically unverified: the rail's real auto-layout rule and its 1024px threshold (needs `get_design_context`, deliberately not invoked); Tablet/Mobile rail card's Figma-side internal decomposition (only Desktop's was drilled into); real-browser hit-testing for the z-index stacking/lift-list on `ZimmProductCard` (jsdom can't do this — the codebase's own tests say so, and no lane re-ran a live-browser check, only cited the team's prior manual ones); whether a real Zimmermann category/CMS path exists whose last segment is literally `cart` (the substring-match edge case in `recommended-products/index.tsx:263`); and whether `cr review --light` was actually run against this session's commits per AGENTS.md's workflow step 4 (not checked — outside this sweep's remit, but worth someone confirming before merge).
